nodes.label: Ten Blocking Passes
nodes.rationale: Union of exact-name, rare-token, address-prefix, postal+name, fallback, name/street prefix-5 and rare-token pair/triple passes keeps recall high while per-pass caps stop common-token blocks dominating.

nodes.label: Candidates Parquet Contract
nodes.rationale: Defines the exact final candidate set (s1_id, cand_id, pass_id, block_score, is_s2) the matcher scores.

nodes.label: D1 Blocking plus classifier, not end-to-end
nodes.norm_label: d1 blocking plus classifier, not end-to-end
nodes.rationale: ~1e13 cross-product is infeasible on local CPU; end-to-end transformer and CPU ANN blocking rejected. Consequence: recall bounded by blocking (0.814).

nodes.label: D10 Leave-one-country-out as France proxy
nodes.rationale: France is ~15% of test with no labels; retraining on one country and validating the other shows a 0.09-0.12 drop, so leaderboard expectation is ~0.80-0.85.

nodes.label: D11 Ship exactly the required submission tree
nodes.norm_label: d11 ship exactly the required submission tree
nodes.rationale: Spec compliance and self-containment: no models/ shipped, a minimal src/config.json lets a reproducer retrain from data.

nodes.label: D2 DuckDB for joins, pandas/pyarrow for the rest
nodes.norm_label: d2 duckdb for joins, pandas/pyarrow for the rest
nodes.rationale: Out-of-core joins over 250-300M pairs within 23 GB RAM; stages restartable via parquet caches.

nodes.label: D3 Ten blocking passes with per-pass caps
nodes.norm_label: d3 ten blocking passes with per-pass caps
nodes.rationale: Exact-name alone recalls only ~22%; shared name-token prefix-5 covers ~89% and >=2 shared tokens ~78%, so prefix and token-pair keys are highest yield. Train recall 0.8115.

nodes.label: D4 Do not reintroduce per-token Metaphone
nodes.norm_label: d4 do not reintroduce per-token metaphone
nodes.rationale: Generic phonetic codes collide massively; removal avoided a 75 GiB temp explosion and recall was recovered via prefix/pair passes.

nodes.label: D5 LightGBM as the matcher
nodes.rationale: Quality tied with XGBoost (identical AUC, F0.5 within 0.0003) but LightGBM trains 3-4.5x faster for local iteration; 610-tree model.

nodes.label: D6 4:1 negative sampling for training
nodes.rationale: Fast training on all positives plus half-hard/half-random country-matched negatives, accepting that sampled thresholds are miscalibrated for full candidates (see D8).

nodes.label: D7 Injective one-to-one post-process
nodes.rationale: Ground truth is injective, so keep only the highest-probability assignment; verified to improve full-candidate macro F0.5 (0.8488 vs 0.8475).

nodes.label: D8 Threshold tuned on full candidates (0.925 not 0.675)
nodes.norm_label: d8 threshold tuned on full candidates (0.925 not 0.675)
nodes.rationale: ~4 negatives per positive in the sample vs ~135 candidates per entity at inference; re-tuning yields better precision (200,982 vs 151,576 singletons).

nodes.label: D9 Full-candidate held-out validation is the reported number
nodes.norm_label: d9 full-candidate held-out validation is the reported number
nodes.rationale: The 4:1 mark (0.9807) is optimistic; 0.8488 (95% CI 0.8481-0.8496) predicted exactly as inference is the believable estimate.

nodes.label: Kaggle-only Cascade (C+B)
nodes.rationale: Precision-first cascade: cheap recall net, GBDT prune, multilingual cross-encoder rerank; every GPU stage optional to the critical path so the classical baseline can ship alone.

nodes.label: Train Candidate Recall = 0.8115
nodes.rationale: US 0.868 vs India 0.727; India trails because Indic names and sparse addresses yield fewer shared rare tokens.

nodes.label: Full-candidate Held-out macro F0.5 = 0.8488
nodes.rationale: Believable in-domain estimate computed on 438,499 held-out S1 groups with their complete candidate sets (95% CI 0.8481-0.8496).

nodes.label: 4:1 Sampled macro F0.5 = 0.9807
nodes.rationale: Optimistic and not leaderboard-comparable because negatives are sampled 4:1 rather than the full candidate distribution.

nodes.label: LOO macro F0.5 = 0.668 / 0.804
nodes.rationale: Unseen-country (France proxy) transfer loses 0.086-0.121 F0.5, giving a realistic leaderboard expectation of ~0.80-0.85.

nodes.label: macro F0.5 (beta=0.5) Metric
nodes.rationale: Precision-heavy, computed per S1 entity with singletons included; false merges are penalised 2x versus missed matches.

nodes.label: Held-out Candidate Recall Ceiling = 0.814
nodes.rationale: Blocking recall bounds the maximum achievable macro F0.5.

nodes.label: Decision Threshold = 0.925
nodes.rationale: Re-tuned on the full candidate distribution (not the 4:1 sample at 0.675) because sampled negatives under-represent confusable candidate mass at inference.

nodes.label: Injective One-to-One Post-process
nodes.rationale: Exploits the measured injective ground truth (each S2/S3 ID in at most one S1 list) to raise precision without external data.

nodes.label: Processed Records Parquet Contract
nodes.rationale: Fixes the normalized column set and ground-truth schema so all downstream stages share one data contract.

nodes.label: Pipeline Stage: audit
nodes.rationale: Measures blocking recall/reduction against ground truth cheaply so pass caps can be tuned without materializing candidate tuples.

nodes.label: Pipeline Stage: block
nodes.rationale: A hard blocking stage bounds the ~1e13 cross-product into a high-recall candidate set; recall is the ceiling for the whole pipeline.

nodes.label: Pipeline Stage: loo (leave-one-country-out)
nodes.rationale: Approximates the zero-shot France split by training on one country and validating on the other.

nodes.label: Pipeline Stage: prepare
nodes.rationale: Stage 0 normalizes/parses all six record files and caches to parquet so every later stage is restartable and memory-bounded.

nodes.label: Pipeline Stage: validation
nodes.rationale: Scores the held-out 20% S1 groups on their full candidate sets (test-like) because 4:1 sampling understates false-merge risk.
